cohort: 112,441 deliveries from 39 hospitals across 14 provinces and autonomous regions in China in 2011.
finding: Low birth weight infants had significantly higher rates of cesarean section, stillbirth, neonatal asphyxia, and mortality compared to normal birth weight infants, but extending gestational age to at least 34 weeks and considering cesarean delivery in specific situations may improve outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were higher for LBW infants compared to NBW infants, and while cesarean delivery for full-term LBW infants was associated with lower stillbirth and neonatal mortality rates compared to vaginal delivery, it did not eliminate complications.
